candidate_identities.comment: Printing Ink Cleaner is used to clean the ink cartridges of a printer. It involves the use of isopropyl alcohol applied to a piece of paper towel, which is then gently rubbed along the print heads on the back or underside of the ink cartridges. This process is repeated several times to adequately remove the ink. Alternatively, scrubbing with soap and cold water can also be used, although this method can be laborious as the soap doesn't actively break up the ink on a molecular level. Hand sanitizer, which contains alcohol, can be used to break up the ink compounds faster.

Conventionally, detergent is used to mean synthetic cleaning compounds as opposed to soap. They are chemically different from soaps but are able to emulsify oils, hold dirt in suspension, and act as wetting agents. Detergents are not prepared from fats and oils, are not inactivated by hard water, and have wetting-agent and emulsifying-agent properties. They are effective even in hard or saltwater, unlike soaps, because they do not develop scum.

candidate_identities.comment: Textile refers to any filament, fiber, or yarn that can be made into fabric or cloth, and the resulting material itself. The term is derived from the Latin textilis and the French texere, meaning 'to weave,' and it originally referred only to woven fabrics. It has, however, come to include fabrics produced by other methods. Textile is an umbrella term that includes various fiber-based materials, including fibers, yarns, filaments, threads, different fabric types, etc.

candidate_identities.comment: Scrap fabric refers to chips, cuttings, fragments, or other small pieces of raw material removed, cut away, flaked off, etc., in the process of making or manufacturing an item. They are often used in sewing projects and can be upcycled into various items such as home decor, accessories, pet toys, and more. There are many creative ways to repurpose these scraps, including making phone cases, monogram pouches, accent pillows, dishtowel belts, marble necklaces, skirts, chapstick holders, cuddle pillows, and mason jars.

candidate_identities.comment: Fabrics waste, or textile wastage, is the material that becomes unusable or worthless after the end of the production process of any textile product. This waste is produced in every stage of the textile manufacturing process such as spinning, weaving, knitting, dyeing, finishing and clothing. The waste created in the textile and garment industry consists of fabrics and trims, including buttons, embroidery threads, and other adornments. It is estimated that 10-25% of fabric is wasted during the cutting process. Waste can also occur due to misprints and embroidery mistakes.

These fuel rods are arranged in bundles (fuel assemblies) in a nuclear reactor and are used to release energy during the nuclear fission process. Under RCRA, only materials that meet the definition of solid waste can be classified as hazardous wastes. In 2018, about 146.1 million tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) were landfilled in the United States, with food being the largest component at about 24 percent, followed by plastics at over 18 percent, and paper and paperboard at about 12 percent. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) defines solid waste as any material that is discarded and not subject to an exclusion or variance, which includes materials that are abandoned, recycled, or inherently waste-like. The EPA also provides information on best practices for waste management and has developed tools for identifying appropriate waste staging and storage.

candidate_identities.comment: Landfill disposal refers to the process of managing and disposing of various types of waste, including municipal solid waste (MSW), construction and demolition debris (C&D), hazardous waste, and coal combustion residuals (CCRs or coal ash). Landfills are well-engineered facilities designed to protect the environment from contaminants present in the solid waste. They are built to hold a wide range of waste, from manufacturing and construction waste to agriculture waste. An industrial waste landfill includes all disposal areas at the facility.

candidate_identities.comment: General solid waste, regulated by the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), is a material that can be classified as hazardous if it meets the definition of solid waste under RCRA. Hazardous waste has the potential to negatively affect human health and the environment, exhibiting characteristics such as ignitability, corrosivity, reactivity, or toxicity. Treatment of waste can render it less toxic, providing more options for transport and disposal. Volume reduction is also a key aspect of waste management.

candidate_identities.comment: Hazardous solid waste is a term used in the hazardous waste management program. It is defined by the EPA's hazardous waste regulations under RCRA Subtitle C. This type of waste can cause substantial harm to human health and the environment if improperly handled. It can take the form of solids, liquids, sludges, or contained gases, and is primarily generated by chemical production, manufacturing, and other industrial activities. A solid waste derived from a hazardous waste is not considered hazardous when it no longer exhibits any characteristic of hazardous waste.

candidate_identities.comment: A waste sheet or waste log is used to document and track waste, particularly in a kitchen setting. It helps managers understand the type, weight, and reasons for food waste. The waste log contains checklists that monitor food movement from the time it was purchased to the time it reached the table. Waste prevention is the most effective method to reduce the environmental impact of wasted food. It stops the creation of unneeded materials and saves money spent on purchasing, handling food, and waste disposal.

Waste residue encompasses different types of waste like municipal solid waste, hazardous waste, industrial non-hazardous waste, agricultural and animal waste, medical waste, radioactive waste, construction and demolition debris, extraction and mining waste, oil and gas production waste, fossil fuel combustion waste, and sewage sludge.

candidate_identities.comment: Waste wire, also known as electronic waste or e-waste, describes discarded electrical or electronic devices. It is often sent to various countries for processing, sometimes illegally. The plastic coating on the wires can release harmful contaminants like lead and dioxins into the environment when exposed to extreme heat and other environmental conditions. Pure copper can be extracted from waste cables and wires by wire stripping machine, water type or dry type copper wire recycling machine.

Abandoned drilling fluid constitutes one of the largest wastes generated during oil and gas exploration and development.

candidate_identities.comment: Solid waste refers to materials regulated by the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) and includes both hazardous and non-hazardous waste. Under RCRA, only materials that meet the definition of solid waste can be classified as hazardous wastes. In 2018, about 146.1 million tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) were landfilled in the United States, with food being the largest component at about 24 percent, followed by plastics at over 18 percent, and paper and paperboard at about 12 percent. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) defines solid waste as any material that is discarded and not subject to an exclusion or variance, which includes materials that are abandoned, recycled, or inherently waste-like. The EPA also provides information on best practices for waste management and has developed tools for identifying appropriate waste staging and storage.

candidate_identities.comment: A concrete slab is a common structural element of modern buildings, consisting of a flat, horizontal surface made of cast concrete. It is typically 4 to 6 inches thick and is used to create floors and ceilings, as well as to provide a level and stable base for outdoor structures like sheds, pergolas, and patios. The process of laying a concrete slab involves building a frame, preparing the base with a layer of sand or gravel, and pouring concrete into the frame. It is important to work quickly due to the concrete's setting time and to ensure a smooth, level finish for the slab's surface.

candidate_identities.comment: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), also known as PTFE or "plastic king", is a polymer synthesized by polymerization of tetrafluoroethylene as a monomer. Its chemical formula is (C2F4) n. It has excellent heat and cold resistance and can be used for a long time at -180~260 º C. This material has the characteristics of acid resistance, alkali resistance, and resistance to various organic solvents, and is almost insoluble in all solvents. Meanwhile, polytetrafluoroethylene has the characteristic of high temperature resistance and extremely low friction coefficient, making it an ideal coating for easy cleaning of the inner layer of water pipes in addition to serving as a lubricant.

candidate_identities.comment: Solid waste refers to materials regulated by the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) and includes both hazardous and non-hazardous waste. Under RCRA, only materials that meet the definition of solid waste can be classified as hazardous wastes. In 2018, about 146.1 million tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) were landfilled in the United States, with food being the largest component at about 24 percent, followed by plastics at over 18 percent, and paper and paperboard at about 12 percent. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) defines solid waste as any material that is discarded and not subject to an exclusion or variance, which includes materials that are abandoned, recycled, or inherently waste-like. The EPA also provides information on best practices for waste management and has developed tools for identifying appropriate waste staging and storage.

Inside the compressor, the lubricant acts to seal the gaps between the screw elements, aiding the compression process.

These contaminants can leach into ground or surface waters, be taken up by plants and animals, contaminate drinking water supplies, or volatilize and affect indoor air quality. Soil contamination can result from pesticides, petroleum products, asbestos, lead, and other hazardous substances. It can be localized or widespread, and is a significant global concern, particularly severe in regions like Europe, Eurasia, Asia, and North Africa. The EPA aims to prevent adverse effects by protecting soil integrity, while the FAO reports that one-third of the world's soil is already severely or moderately degraded.

candidate_identities.comment: Humic acids are organic compounds that can be extracted from peat, leonardite, and soil. They are obtained through an alkaline extraction process and are known for their role in improving soil quality and plant growth. They are distinct from fulvic acids, which are soluble at all pH levels, whereas humic acids are not. Humic acids are considered excellent soil amendments due to their ability to neutralize soil acidity and fortify cell membranes.

candidate_identities.comment: A softener is a device that eliminates hard water without losing health benefits, maintaining some levels of calcium and magnesium. candidate_identities.comment: Liquid detergent is a type of laundry detergent that is better for oil and grease stains, sensitive skin, and hand washing. It works better in cold water, is easier to measure, and can be used as spot treatments or when hand-washing clothes. It can be used for any kind of washing, but delivers its best when used to clean oily stains, and/or in areas with hard water. Liquid detergents possess a higher ability to release and break down fat, and their ingredients are resilient to minerals typically found in hard water.

candidate_identities.comment: Textile refers to any filament, fiber, or yarn that can be made into fabric or cloth, and the resulting material itself. The term is derived from the Latin textilis and the French texere, meaning 'to weave,' and it originally referred only to woven fabrics. Textile is an umbrella term that includes various fiber-based materials, including fibers, yarns, filaments, threads, different fabric types, etc.

candidate_identities.comment: Fabrics waste, or textile wastage, is the material that becomes unusable or worthless after the end of the production process of any textile product. This waste is produced in every stage of the textile manufacturing process such as spinning, weaving, knitting, dyeing, finishing and clothing. The waste created in the textile and garment industry consists of fabrics and trims, including buttons, embroidery threads, and other adornments. It is estimated that 10-25% of fabric is wasted during the cutting process. Waste can also occur due to misprints and embroidery mistakes.

candidate_identities.comment: Activated Coke is a form of carbon derived primarily from coal, though it can also be produced from other carbonaceous materials. It is treated or 'activated' to increase its surface area and porosity, enhancing its ability to adsorb gases and solutes. This process typically involves heating the material in the presence of gases that chemically react with the carbon, creating a highly porous structure. Activated coke is particularly effective in adsorbing pollutants and contaminants from gas streams, making it valuable in environmental applications such as air purification and industrial emission control. Its high surface area also makes it useful in chemical processes and as a catalyst support.

candidate_identities.comment: Antifreeze is a functional liquid made by mixing ethylene glycol, propylene glycol or glycerol as the core base liquid with functional additives such as corrosion inhibitors, preservatives, defoamers and scale inhibitors, and water in a specific proportion (usually 30%-70% of the base liquid). The core features are wide temperature range adaptability - the freezing point can be as low as -10 ℃ to -60℃ (to meet the needs of different cold regions), and the boiling point is above 100℃ (to prevent boiling under high-temperature conditions). At the same time, it has excellent anti-corrosion, anti-scaling and anti-rust performance, which can protect metal pipelines (such as steel, aluminum and copper) and rubber sealing parts from erosion. Moreover, it has strong chemical stability, good fluidity, and can also have a lubricating effect to reduce the wear of the pump body in the cooling system. Its application scenarios are extensive, covering automotive engine cooling systems, industrial equipment (such as compressors and heat exchangers), new energy facilities (wind turbine naceling cooling systems, hydraulic systems, photovoltaic inverter heat dissipation circuits), heating pipes and outdoor equipment, etc. The core function is to prevent pipe freezing and cracking in low-temperature environments, while efficiently dissipating heat in high-temperature conditions. To ensure the stable operation of the equipment under extreme temperatures, when in use, the corresponding freezing point specification should be selected based on the ambient temperature, and the mixing of different types of antifreeze should be avoided.

Multiphase extraction (MPE) is a physical remediation method used for treating contaminated soil and groundwater, particularly effective against halogenated volatile organic compounds (VOCs). It involves the use of a vacuum to remove a combination of impacted groundwater, free phase, and vapors from the subsurface. The extracted materials are then separated and treated above ground. MPE's efficiency depends on the optimization of operating conditions and can rehabilitate both saturated and unsaturated soil zones. It is often compared with traditional remediation methods to evaluate cost and performance.

candidate_identities.comment: NdFeB magnet is a high-performance rare earth permanent magnetic material with neodymium, iron and boron as its core components, and can be modified by adding rare earth elements such as praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium. It is one of the permanent magnetic materials with the highest magnetic energy product and coercivity in commercial applications at present. It features high magnetic strength, small volume and light weight. Meanwhile, through composition optimization, its thermal stability can be improved to adapt to medium and high-temperature working conditions. However, its corrosion resistance is relatively weak and usually requires surface protection treatments such as galvanizing, electrophoresis, and phosphating. This material is widely used in new energy, electronic information, aerospace and other fields. Especially in the wind power field, it is a core component of permanent magnet direct drive wind turbine generators, which can achieve efficient conversion of wind energy to electrical energy through stable strong magnetic fields. It can also be used in new energy vehicle drive motors, precision instrument magnets, variable frequency air conditioning compressors and other equipment. It is a key strategic material that supports the high-performance and lightweight development of new energy equipment.

The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) defines solid waste as any material that is discarded and not subject to an exclusion or variance, which includes materials that are abandoned, recycled, or inherently waste-like. candidate_identities.comment: Anionic surfactants are macromolecules, usually in the sulfonate or sulfate group of chemicals, that act as active surface agents to lower the surface tension of liquids. They work best to remove dirt, clay, and some oily stains. When added to water, they ionize and have a negative charge, allowing them to bind to positively charged particles like clay and impurities suspended in the liquid. They are used in cleaning products to reduce surface tension and wash away oil and grease. However, they are associated with skin irritation.

candidate_identities.comment: Printing ink cleaner is used to clean the printhead of a printer, which helps transfer ink onto the page by firing tiny droplets of ink via numerous printer nozzles. When these nozzles get clogged, prints appear faded or streaky. The simplest method of cleaning is scrubbing with soap and cold water. However, a more effective method involves using a solution containing alcohol, such as hand sanitizer, which breaks up the ink compounds. Another method involves using isopropyl alcohol applied to a piece of paper towel, which is then gently rubbed along the print heads on the back or underside of the ink cartridges.

candidate_identities.comment: Detergent is a surfactant or a mixture of surfactants with cleansing properties when in dilute solutions. Conventionally, detergent is used to mean synthetic cleaning compounds as opposed to soap. They are chemically different from soaps but are able to emulsify oils, hold dirt in suspension, and act as wetting agents. Detergents are not prepared from fats and oils, are not inactivated by hard water, and have wetting-agent and emulsifying-agent properties. They are effective even in hard or saltwater, unlike soaps, because they do not develop scum.

candidate_identities.comment: Fabrics waste, or textile wastage, is the material that becomes unusable or worthless after the end of the production process of any textile product. This waste is produced in every stage of the textile manufacturing process such as spinning, weaving, knitting, dyeing, finishing and clothing. Gas oil refers to a fraction obtained by the fractional distillation of crude oil or other secondary processed oils in an oil refinery, with a boiling point range of 200-380°C. Note 1: This distillate oil can be used for blending vehicle gas oil, heating oil, and marine distillate fuel.
Note 2: It refers to atmospheric gas oil (AGO) or vacuum gas oil (VGO) generally within the distillation range of 250°C to 500°C; VGO is also known as straight-run wax oil.

candidate_identities.comment: Bionatural gas and biogas are a mixture of gases produced through the fermentation of organic matter by microorganisms under anaerobic conditions. Bionatural gas is made from various types of urban and rural organic waste such as crop straw, livestock and poultry manure, kitchen waste, and agricultural and sideline product processing wastewater. Biogas, as the name suggests, is the gas in a swamp. The main component of biogas is methane. Biogas is composed of gases such as 50% -80% methane (CH4), 20% -40% carbon dioxide (CO2), 0% -5% nitrogen (N2), less than 1% hydrogen (H2), less than 0.4% oxygen (O2), and 0.1% -3% hydrogen sulfide (H2S). The calorific value of pure methane per cubic meter is 34000 kilojoules, and the calorific value of biogas per cubic meter is approximately 20800-23600 kilojoules.

candidate_identities.comment: NdFeB magnet is a high-performance rare earth permanent magnetic material with neodymium, iron and boron as its core components, and can be modified by adding rare earth elements such as praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium. It is one of the permanent magnetic materials with the highest magnetic energy product and coercivity in commercial applications at present. It features high magnetic strength, small volume and light weight. Meanwhile, through composition optimization, its thermal stability can be improved to adapt to medium and high-temperature working conditions. However, its corrosion resistance is relatively weak and usually requires surface protection treatments such as galvanizing, electrophoresis, and phosphating. This material is widely used in new energy, electronic information, aerospace and other fields. Especially in the wind power field, it is a core component of permanent magnet direct drive wind turbine generators, which can achieve efficient conversion of wind energy to electrical energy through stable strong magnetic fields. It can also be used in new energy vehicle drive motors, precision instrument magnets, variable frequency air conditioning compressors and other equipment. It is a key strategic material that supports the high-performance and lightweight development of new energy equipment.

candidate_identities.comment: A softener is a device that eliminates hard water without losing health benefits, maintaining some levels of calcium and magnesium. This salt-free softener is ideal for those with high-sodium diets who need to eliminate hard water but don't want to reduce mineral intake. They remove heavy minerals like calcium, iron, and magnesium from the water supply as it enters the home.

candidate_identities.comment: Liquid detergent is a type of laundry detergent that is better for oil and grease stains, sensitive skin, and hand washing. It works better in cold water, is easier to measure, and can be used as spot treatments or when hand-washing clothes. candidate_identities.comment: Soap and detergent are substances that, when dissolved in water, have the ability to remove dirt from surfaces such as human skin, textiles, and other solids. They are essential for maintaining hygiene and cleanliness. While often used interchangeably, soap and detergent differ chemically. Soaps are traditionally made from natural ingredients like animal fat and lye, whereas detergents can be made from synthetic chemicals and may include enzymes for stain removal. The choice between liquid, pods, or powder detergents depends on individual needs and preferences.

candidate_identities.comment: Detergent is a surfactant or a mixture of surfactants with cleansing properties when in dilute solutions. Conventionally, detergent is used to mean synthetic cleaning compounds as opposed to soap. They are chemically different from soaps but are able to emulsify oils, hold dirt in suspension, and act as wetting agents. Detergents are not prepared from fats and oils, are not inactivated by hard water, and have wetting-agent and emulsifying-agent properties. They are effective even in hard or saltwater, unlike soaps, because they do not develop scum.

candidate_identities.comment: Printing Ink Cleaner is used to clean the ink cartridges of a printer. It involves the use of isopropyl alcohol applied to a piece of paper towel, which is then gently rubbed along the print heads on the back or underside of the ink cartridges. This process is repeated several times to adequately remove the ink. Alternatively, scrubbing with soap and cold water can also be used, although this method can be laborious as the soap doesn't actively break up the ink on a molecular level. Hand sanitizer, which contains alcohol, can be used to break up the ink compounds faster.

candidate_identities.comment: NdFeB magnet is a high-performance rare earth permanent magnetic material with neodymium, iron and boron as its core components, and can be modified by adding rare earth elements such as praseodymium, dysprosium and terbium. It is one of the permanent magnetic materials with the highest magnetic energy product and coercivity in commercial applications at present. It features high magnetic strength, small volume and light weight. Meanwhile, through composition optimization, its thermal stability can be improved to adapt to medium and high-temperature working conditions. However, its corrosion resistance is relatively weak and usually requires surface protection treatments such as galvanizing, electrophoresis, and phosphating. This material is widely used in new energy, electronic information, aerospace and other fields. Especially in the wind power field, it is a core component of permanent magnet direct drive wind turbine generators, which can achieve efficient conversion of wind energy to electrical energy through stable strong magnetic fields. It can also be used in new energy vehicle drive motors, precision instrument magnets, variable frequency air conditioning compressors and other equipment. It is a key strategic material that supports the high-performance and lightweight development of new energy equipment.

It is treated or 'activated' to increase its surface area and porosity, enhancing its ability to adsorb gases and solutes. This process typically involves heating the material in the presence of gases that chemically react with the carbon, creating a highly porous structure. Activated coke is particularly effective in adsorbing pollutants and contaminants from gas streams, making it valuable in environmental applications such as air purification and industrial emission control. Its high surface area also makes it useful in chemical processes and as a catalyst support.

Nickel and Cobalt Alloy is a metallic alloy primarily composed of nickel, cobalt, and other elements such as chromium, copper, iron, titanium, and molybdenum. It is known for its toughness, being more than 100 times tougher than graphene. The alloy was particularly used in electroplated coatings during a period of nickel scarcity due to miners' strikes. Cobalt was used as a costly but useful metal to replace nickel in proportions up to 50%.

candidate_identities.comment: Total Suspended Particulate (TSP) refers to microscopic particles of solid or liquid matter suspended in the air. TSP is measured in micrograms per cubic meter of air (µg/m3) and is determined by a gravimetric method using a sampler with a downward pointing tube and a face velocity of 0.5 m/sec. The annual standard level is defined to one decimal place, such as 15.0 µg/m3. TSP includes all airborne particles and is related to other particulate matter measurements such as PM10 and PM2.5. Sources of TSP can be both natural and anthropogenic, and it is an important component in assessing air quality and environmental health.

candidate_identities.comment: Fabrics waste, or textile wastage, is the material that becomes unusable or worthless after the end of the production process of any textile product. This waste is produced in every stage of the textile manufacturing process such as spinning, weaving, knitting, dyeing, finishing and clothing. The waste created in the textile and garment industry consists of fabrics and trims, including buttons, embroidery threads, and other adornments. It is estimated that 10-25% of fabric is wasted during the cutting process. Waste can also occur due to misprints and embroidery mistakes.

There are many creative ways to repurpose these scraps, including making phone cases, monogram pouches, accent pillows, dishtowel belts, marble necklaces, skirts, chapstick holders, cuddle pillows, and mason jars.

candidate_identities.comment: Modified starches are used as food additives for thickening, stabilizing, or emulsifying. They are prepared by physically, enzymatically, or chemically treating native starch to change its properties. This treatment improves its texture and structure for food products that need to be microwaved, freeze-dried, cooked or baked. Modified food starch is a complex carbohydrate that has had one or more of its components altered to give it a more desirable texture, helps it hold up well against heat and acidic environments, and helps it dissolve faster.

candidate_identities.comment: Food debris refers to material, especially carbohydrates, fats, and proteins, that an organism uses for energy, growth, and maintaining the processes of life. It is food that is intended for human consumption that is wasted and lost, and can occur anywhere throughout the entire supply chain from farm stage to harvest to households. The causes of food waste or loss are numerous and occur throughout the food system, during production, processing, distribution, retail and food service sales, and consumption.

candidate_identities.comment: Waste residue refers to secondary renewable, bio-based, or biogenic materials not intended as the primary outcome of industrial and commercial processes. It includes a variety of materials such as paper/cardboard, plastics, glass, aluminum, batteries, electronics, food, lawn materials, used oil, household hazardous waste, tires, metal, and miscellaneous items. Waste residue encompasses different types of waste like municipal solid waste, hazardous waste, industrial non-hazardous waste, agricultural and animal waste, medical waste, radioactive waste, construction and demolition debris, extraction and mining waste, oil and gas production waste, fossil fuel combustion waste, and sewage sludge.

candidate_identities.comment: Solid waste refers to materials regulated by the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) and includes both hazardous and non-hazardous waste. Under RCRA, only materials that meet the definition of solid waste can be classified as hazardous wastes. In 2018, about 146.1 million tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) were landfilled in the United States, with food being the largest component at about 24 percent, followed by plastics at over 18 percent, and paper and paperboard at about 12 percent. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) defines solid waste as any material that is discarded and not subject to an exclusion or variance, which includes materials that are abandoned, recycled, or inherently waste-like. The EPA also provides information on best practices for waste management and has developed tools for identifying appropriate waste staging and storage.

candidate_identities.comment: Organic fertilizers feed the soil and sustain plants. They include animal waste and byproducts, such as bird and bat guano, blood meal, bone meal and feather meal, as well as fish and kelp fertilizers. Organic fertilizers depend on soil microbes to release macronutrients such as nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K) gradually over time. They improve soil structure and enhance the natural fertility of the soil or replace chemical elements taken from the soil by previous crops.

Glues and gelatine, peptones and their derivatives, and related products; caseinates and other casein derivatives; albuminates and other albumin derivatives

candidate_identities.comment: Bone glue is a type of adhesive that was used by ancient civilizations for various tasks. It is made from animal bones, water, and a source of heat. The bones are crushed into a very fine powder to make the glue. It is a synthetic carbonated hydroxyapatite with a carbonate ion content similar to bone mineral. This calcium/phosphate mixture hardens into dahllite 5 minutes post mixing, acting as 'instant bone' for fractures. It sets up relatively quickly after it is applied and becomes jelly-like and will no longer bond if allowed to cool.

In 2018, about 146.1 million tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) were landfilled in the United States, with food being the largest component at about 24 percent, followed by plastics at over 18 percent, and paper and paperboard at about 12 percent. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) defines solid waste as any material that is discarded and not subject to an exclusion or variance, which includes materials that are abandoned, recycled, or inherently waste-like. The EPA also provides information on best practices for waste management and has developed tools for identifying appropriate waste staging and storage.

candidate_identities.comment: Fabrics waste, or textile wastage, is the material that becomes unusable or worthless after the end of the production process of any textile product. This waste is produced in every stage of the textile manufacturing process such as spinning, weaving, knitting, dyeing, finishing and clothing. The waste created in the textile and garment industry consists of fabrics and trims, including buttons, embroidery threads, and other adornments. It is estimated that 10-25% of fabric is wasted during the cutting process. Waste can also occur due to misprints and embroidery mistakes.

candidate_identities.comment: Solid waste refers to materials regulated by the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) and includes both hazardous and non-hazardous waste. Under RCRA, only materials that meet the definition of solid waste can be classified as hazardous wastes. In 2018, about 146.1 million tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) were landfilled in the United States, with food being the largest component at about 24 percent, followed by plastics at over 18 percent, and paper and paperboard at about 12 percent. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) defines solid waste as any material that is discarded and not subject to an exclusion or variance, which includes materials that are abandoned, recycled, or inherently waste-like. The EPA also provides information on best practices for waste management and has developed tools for identifying appropriate waste staging and storage.

It affects the color of candlelight and is a mixture of solid particles and liquid droplets in the air.

candidate_identities.comment: Soap and detergent are substances that, when dissolved in water, have the ability to remove dirt from surfaces such as human skin, textiles, and other solids. They are essential for maintaining hygiene and cleanliness. While often used interchangeably, soap and detergent differ chemically. Soaps are traditionally made from natural ingredients like animal fat and lye, whereas detergents can be made from synthetic chemicals and may include enzymes for stain removal. The choice between liquid, pods, or powder detergents depends on individual needs and preferences.

candidate_identities.comment: Detergent is a surfactant or a mixture of surfactants with cleansing properties when in dilute solutions. Conventionally, detergent is used to mean synthetic cleaning compounds as opposed to soap. They are chemically different from soaps but are able to emulsify oils, hold dirt in suspension, and act as wetting agents. Detergents are not prepared from fats and oils, are not inactivated by hard water, and have wetting-agent and emulsifying-agent properties. They are effective even in hard or saltwater, unlike soaps, because they do not develop scum.

candidate_identities.comment: Liquid detergent is a type of laundry detergent that is better for oil and grease stains, sensitive skin, and hand washing. It works better in cold water, is easier to measure, and can be used as spot treatments or when hand-washing clothes. It can be used for any kind of washing, but delivers its best when used to clean oily stains, and/or in areas with hard water. Liquid detergents possess a higher ability to release and break down fat, and their ingredients are resilient to minerals typically found in hard water.

candidate_identities.comment: Plastic waste refers to the discarded materials made of plastic that accumulate in the environment. Plastics are a significant part of municipal solid waste, with containers and packaging being the largest contributors. In 2018, over 14.5 million tons of plastic waste were generated from packaging alone. Recycling of plastic waste involves the recovery and transformation of plastic materials to create new products, reducing the need for virgin raw materials and helping to protect the environment from pollution and greenhouse gas emissions. Despite the benefits, recycling rates for plastics are lower compared to materials like aluminum, glass, and paper.

candidate_identities.comment: Drilling waste is an unavoidable consequence of drilling operations, produced when drilling fluids mix with cuttings and cavings. During drilling, a mixture of oil, gas, and formation water is pumped to the surface. The water is separated into tanks or pits, referred to as 'produced water'. Wastes generated from crude oil and natural gas exploration and production are regulated under the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) and state regulations. Abandoned drilling fluid constitutes one of the largest wastes generated during oil and gas exploration and development.

candidate_identities.comment: Solid waste refers to materials regulated by the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA) and includes both hazardous and non-hazardous waste. Under RCRA, only materials that meet the definition of solid waste can be classified as hazardous wastes. In 2018, about 146.1 million tons of municipal solid waste (MSW) were landfilled in the United States, with food being the largest component at about 24 percent, followed by plastics at over 18 percent, and paper and paperboard at about 12 percent. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) defines solid waste as any material that is discarded and not subject to an exclusion or variance, which includes materials that are abandoned, recycled, or inherently waste-like. The EPA also provides information on best practices for waste management and has developed tools for identifying appropriate waste staging and storage.

candidate_identities.comment: Waste residue refers to secondary renewable, bio-based, or biogenic materials not intended as the primary outcome of industrial and commercial processes. It includes a variety of materials such as paper/cardboard, plastics, glass, aluminum, batteries, electronics, food, lawn materials, used oil, household hazardous waste, tires, metal, and miscellaneous items. Waste residue encompasses different types of waste like municipal solid waste, hazardous waste, industrial non-hazardous waste, agricultural and animal waste, medical waste, radioactive waste, construction and demolition debris, extraction and mining waste, oil and gas production waste, fossil fuel combustion waste, and sewage sludge.

candidate_identities.comment: Waste wire, also known as electronic waste or e-waste, describes discarded electrical or electronic devices. It is often sent to various countries for processing, sometimes illegally. The plastic coating on the wires can release harmful contaminants like lead and dioxins into the environment when exposed to extreme heat and other environmental conditions. Pure copper can be extracted from waste cables and wires by wire stripping machine, water type or dry type copper wire recycling machine.

candidate_identities.comment: Hazardous solid waste is a term used in the hazardous waste management program. It is defined by the EPA's hazardous waste regulations under RCRA Subtitle C. This type of waste can cause substantial harm to human health and the environment if improperly handled. It can take the form of solids, liquids, sludges, or contained gases, and is primarily generated by chemical production, manufacturing, and other industrial activities. A solid waste derived from a hazardous waste is not considered hazardous when it no longer exhibits any characteristic of hazardous waste.

candidate_identities.comment: General solid waste, regulated by the Resource Conservation and Recovery Act (RCRA), is a material that can be classified as hazardous if it meets the definition of solid waste under RCRA. Hazardous waste has the potential to negatively affect human health and the environment, exhibiting characteristics such as ignitability, corrosivity, reactivity, or toxicity. Treatment of waste can render it less toxic, providing more options for transport and disposal. Volume reduction is also a key aspect of waste management.

candidate_identities.comment: Waste rubber, predominantly sourced from rubber tires of automobiles, trucks, and motorcycles, is a significant environmental issue due to its durability and large volume. Other sources include clothing, footwear, and miscellaneous durable and nondurable products. The disposal of waste rubber is challenging as the material takes several years to degrade. Vulcanized rubbers, a type of waste rubber, are extensively used in various applications due to their mechanical strength and durability. However, recycling waste rubber is difficult due to its durability, large volume, and the hazards involved in its handling and storage.

candidate_identities.comment: Liquid waste is a major problem globally, with it being defined as any waste material that qualifies as a 'liquid'. It is extremely hazardous as unlike solid waste, it cannot be easily removed. This waste material is classified into two types: inorganic and organic waste. It is typically generated from industrial processes such as manufacturing and power generation, and from activities like cleaning and sanitizing. It includes such liquids as wastewater, fats, oils or grease (FOG), used oil, liquids, solids, gases, sludges and hazardous household liquids.

candidate_identities.comment: Construction waste consists of materials generated when new buildings and civil-engineering structures are built, renovated, or demolished. This includes materials such as wood, metal, concrete, plastic, asphalt, and other debris. Construction waste can be hazardous and can have a negative impact on the environment if not disposed of properly. Construction waste management involves reducing waste generated on a construction site and disposing of it in an environmentally friendly and safe manner.

candidate_identities.comment: Elementary flow for particulate matter emitted to air, unspecified subcompartment, where the particle-size fraction is not specified. The reference property is mass, expressed in kilograms. No particular particle-size distribution, chemical composition, stack height or LCIA characterization factor is assigned by this Flow definition. Source context retained from the preceding version: Song et al. (2021), DOI 10.13671/j.hjkxxb.2021.0276, reports 0.01689 kg/t of particulate-matter emissions from clinker preheating and calcination after dust collection, without reporting particle size. This is a source-specific application example, not the amount per kilogram of this Flow or a requirement that all uses represent the same treatment technology. Actual emissions, controls and source evidence belong to the corresponding Process exchange; characterization coverage is assessed for the exact Flow and the selected LCIA method.
